previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A 60-year-old male with a history of kidney transplantation, stage 4 chronic kidney disease, heart failure with preserved ejection fraction, atrial fibrillation, and recent hospitalization for pleural effusion was readmitted for acute dyspnea. Imaging revealed a recurrent, loculated right pleural effusion, prompting VATS decortication and chest tube placement. He developed postoperative bleeding requiring transfusion and was treated for a complicated Citrobacter koseri urinary tract infection despite being asymptomatic, due to immunosuppression. His heart failure was managed with diuresis, and his tacrolimus dose was adjusted based on trough levels. He was weaned off oxygen, stabilized, and discharged to extended care for rehabilitation with plans for outpatient follow-up, sleep study, and continued antibiotic and immunosuppressive therapy.

ACUTE ISSUES
============
#Cough 
Presented with predominant symptom of cough that had developed 
over the prior ___ days with a leukocytosis to 12.9. CT CHEST on 
___ suspicious for atypical pneumonia vs aspiration 
pneumonitis with LLL airspace opacities.  Patient was seen by 
both infectious disease teams and pulmonary teams given his 
immunosuppression and concern for atypical infection.  
Antibiotics were deferred given resolution of cough and 
leukocytosis while work-up was pursued. Further incentive to 
defer abx with history of recurrent C. difficile infection s/p 
FMT. Pertinent workup included negative urinary strep and 
Legionella antigens, negative cryptococcal antigen, blood 
cultures no growth.  Galactomannan and beta glucan pending at 
time of discharge. Sputum culture also pending at time of 
discharge.  Cough may have been due to a viral upper respiratory 
tract infection that was unrelated to the CT findings; however, 
given his complicated medical history, plan to follow-up with 
infectious disease teams and pulmonary teams as an outpatient 
for follow-up imaging and further evaluation.

#Asymptomatic bacteriuria
Ucx grew CITROBACTER KOSERI. >100,000 CFU/mL and ENTEROCOCCUS SP 
10,000-100,000 CFU/mL.  Patient had no symptoms.  Patient 
several years out from transplantation; colonization therefore a
